verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 5.6% to $190.7B and its store operating profit grew 10.8% — but a $2.1B paper loss on its investment stakes cut headline profit 19% to $4.2B.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The big U.S. stores — net sales up 4.6%, comparable sales up 4.6%, eCommerce up 27%.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and e-commerce outside the U.S., including Flipkart in India — growth led by China, Walmex and Flipkart; up 7.5% in constant currency.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: The warehouse-club business — net sales up 2.9%, or 4.0% excluding fuel.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Sam's Club membership fees plus advertising (Walmart Connect in the U.S. grew 41%) and other income.

opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, the supply chain and the back office.

otherDetail: Interest of $621M, net, plus a $2,117M loss on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value declines. A year ago that investments line was a $294M loss.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $4,237M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $4,392M, of which $155M belongs to noncontrolling interests.
follow100Note: Walmart keeps just $2.22 of every $100 — but on $190.7B of quarterly revenue that is still $4.2B. This quarter $1.44 of every $100 went to paper losses on investment stakes; the stores themselves earned 10.8% more than a year ago.

takeaways.title: Stores earned faster than sales
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 10.8% to $8.7B — twice the pace of sales — as gross margin improved and eCommerce economics got better, led by Walmart U.S. and International.

takeaways.title: Paper losses cut the headline
takeaways.text: A $2,117M loss on equity and other investments turned a strong store quarter into a 19% decline in headline profit. Adjusted EPS, which strips the loss out, was $0.74 versus GAAP EPS of $0.53.

takeaways.title: New buyback, bigger dividend
takeaways.text: Walmart announced a new $30B share-repurchase authorization in February 2026 and raised its annual dividend to $0.99 per share.

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $2,117M loss — mostly fair-value moves on equity investments (a year ago it was a $294M loss). Adjusted EPS of $0.74 excludes a $0.21 net-of-tax loss from these items.
Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale shifted on the calendar — nine days fell in Q3 this year versus five last year — which moved some International sales out of the fourth quarter.
